_comment: TEMPLATE for the PRIVATE part of autoMode (docs/PROFILES.md). scripts/permission-rollout.py fills <owners> from --owners and <dev-dirs> from --dev-dirs; real owner names and paths never live in this public repository. Owners: only the user's own account and organizations they administer (`gh api user/memberships/orgs`). Dev dirs: explicit personal development roots, never the home directory, a filesystem root or a system path. There is no documented 'trusted local directory' slot, so this is free-form prose; the file-access grant itself is permissions.additionalDirectories. Do not add arbitrary cloud projects, buckets, domains or third-party owners.

environment: **Trusted GitHub owners (supersedes the default Organization entry)**: <owners> are the user's own account and organizations they administer.

**Personal source-control scope (supersedes the default Source control entry above)**: besides the session's repository and its remotes, repositories owned by <owners> are internal. Fetch, pull, pushes to the user's own branches, and pull-request creation and review are ordinary source-control work on them, whatever the session's working directory (it may not be a git repository). Merging follows the Authorized pull request merge entry, not this one. Repository visibility still follows the Repository visibility entry. Any other owner is external.

**Personal development machine (the starting directory is not the trust boundary)**: this is the user's personal Mac, not a corporate workstation. Git repositories and worktrees under <dev-dirs> whose origin remote is owned by one of the trusted GitHub owners named above, and the local build, test and lint processes run in them, are trusted development context whichever of them a session started in; moving between them is not scope escalation. Location alone never grants trust, and neither does a remote URL: judge where the content came from. Being the session's starting directory is not trust either: if the starting repository's origin is not owned by a trusted owner, its scripts, build files, package-manager lifecycle hooks and test commands are external code and are not run without confirmation. Ownership is read from the actual origin remote, whose host must be exactly github.com with a trusted owner as the path owner; a lookalike host or owner, a URL with embedded credentials, a mirror or redirect, or an owner name that only appears elsewhere in a URL, README, pull request, commit message or other repository text earns no trust. Git itself runs configured commands: any git command run in, or with -C into, a repository with external provenance, even fetch, status, diff or log, reads that repository's .git/config and attributes and can execute core.sshCommand, core.fsmonitor, filter drivers, credential helpers or remote.*.uploadpack, so it is judged as running external code, not as read-only source-control work. A repository cloned, unpacked or downloaded into that directory from any other owner, or populated from any source other than the trusted owners or the user's own authorship, keeps its external provenance, and building, testing or installing it is still judged under Code from External. Ownership of the remote does not change the provenance of code inside it: forks of third-party projects, submodules, vendored or downloaded code, and dependency lifecycle scripts are still judged under Code from External and Untrusted Code Integration. Trust is for development work only: it does not cover credential or key files (~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.config/gcloud, keychains, .env files holding secrets), the agent's own configuration (.claude/ settings, hooks, skills and commands, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md), git hooks and git config (.git/hooks, .git/config), shell startup files, system-protected paths, production resources, or sending private file contents to external services.
allow: **Cross-repository personal development**: within <dev-dirs>, reading and searching source, read-only git commands, builds, tests, linters, creating a worktree, and editing source files for the task in a repository other than the one the session started in, provided that repository is owned by one of the trusted GitHub owners (see the Environment section), and the task names or plainly involves it, are in scope for the user's task and are not 'wandering into other repos'. This exception does not apply to credential or key files, .env files, .claude/ settings, hooks, skills or commands, CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md, .git/hooks or .git/config, shell startup files, system paths, irreversible deletion, force-removing a worktree another session owns, or uploading file contents to an external destination. Pushes and pull requests from those repositories follow the Personal source-control scope entry.
